No programming knowledge needed
Run in class, any day in the window

eligibility.en: Pupils from CM1 (age ~9) to terminale in French schools, including French schools abroad; entered by a teacher-coordinator.

en: Teacher registers as coordinator on castor-informatique.fr
Pick a session date between 8 Nov and 19 Dec 2026
Take the 45-minute contest online in class

costs.en: Free.

score_reason: Huge free contest, French-language

summary.ar: مسابقة ينظمها النظام الأوروبي للبنوك المركزية تؤدي فيها فرق المدارس الثانوية دور محافظي البنوك المركزية: الإجابة عن اختبار في السياسة النقدية، وكتابة قرار بشأن أسعار الفائدة وعرضه أمام البنك المركزي. وفي لوكسمبورغ تستمر الجولة الأولى حتى 17 نوفمبر 2026.

about.en:
The Generation €uro Students' Award helps students understand how monetary policy works. Teams of students with a teacher complete an online quiz (Round 1), write an essay forecasting the ECB Governing Council's next interest-rate decision (Round 2, to 3 February 2027), and present it to a jury at the central bank (Round 3).

The edition on this page is an initiative of the Banque centrale du Luxembourg and the Banque de France; winners receive prizes announced on the site.

en: Play central banker for a year
Quiz, essay and jury presentation
Free, school teams with a teacher

eligibility.en: Teams of secondary-school students (usually final years) with a teacher at schools in Luxembourg (separate national editions exist in other euro-area countries).

en: Form a team with an economics teacher
Sign up on generationeuro.eu (Luxembourg page)
Complete the Round 1 quiz by 17 Nov 2026
Write the Round 2 assignment by 3 Feb 2027

costs.en: Free.

score_reason: Unique ECB economics contest; Luxembourg schools

Teams of 3–4 compete in online qualifying rounds and state competitions, with top teams advancing to the national semifinals and finals.

It is the leading US high-school economics team competition and a strong signal for economics and business applicants.

Team-based, online qualifiers
National finals for top teams

eligibility.en: Teams of US high-school students with a teacher advisor.

en: Sign up for updates on the CEE page

Register when your state opens (Nov 2026–Jan 2027)

about.en:
The ICO first round has two parts: ZIO, a written problem-solving exam at centres across India, and ZCO, a programming exam. Qualifiers from either sit INOI (the national olympiad, C++), and the top students attend the IOI Training Camp, which selects India's team for IOI 2027 in Germany.

There is no lower age limit; students must still be in school (Class 12 or below).

en: Two entry routes: written ZIO or programming ZCO
Pathway to IOI 2027
Open to all school boards

eligibility.en: Students registered in school up to Class 12 in India (any board), no lower age limit.

en: Register for ZIO/ZCO on the IARCS site
Practise with past ZIO/ZCO papers
Sit ZIO on 21 Nov 2026 and/or ZCO on 12 Dec 2026
Qualify for INOI in early 2027

costs.en: Registration fee per exam (see IARCS announcement).

score_reason: Official IOI route for India; dates soon

The Wiskunde Olympiade challenges secondary students with playful but demanding problems that test creativity and insight. After the first round in schools, the best students advance to a second round at universities and the national final; finalists can join the training programme for the IMO, EGMO and BxMO teams.

Schools register via the competition site; materials are in Dutch.

Path to IMO, EGMO and BxMO teams
Free for students

eligibility.en: Students at secondary schools in the Netherlands (and Dutch-curriculum schools), registered by their school.

en: Ask your maths teacher to register the school by 7 Jan 2027

about.en:
The OII is promoted by the Italian Ministry of Education. Schools register on olimpiadi-scientifiche.it; students sit a school selection round, then territorial (regional) contests, and the best go to the national final, from which the IOI team is trained and chosen. A team championship (OIS) runs alongside.

Participation is free for both schools and students. All materials are in Italian.

en: Free for schools and students
School → regional → national rounds
Selects Italy's IOI team

eligibility.en: Upper-secondary students at Italian schools, registered by their school.

en: Ask your school to register on olimpiadi-scientifiche.it
Train on the official training platform
Sit the school round, then regional and national rounds

costs.en: Free.

about.en:
The Olimpiada Matematyczna is one of Europe's oldest and strongest maths olympiads. The first stage has a test part and an open, proof-based part; qualifiers sit the regional second stage and the national final, and the best are trained for the IMO and EGMO teams.

A scientific camp for top students follows in late May/early June 2027. Problems and solutions are in Polish.

Three stages, Nov 2026 to Mar 2027
Path to IMO and EGMO

USAEBO is the only pathway for US K-12 students to Team USA at the International Economics Olympiad (IEO); in 2026 Team USA won gold, silver and bronze at the IEO in Shenzhen. Rounds cover economic theory, business case analysis and financial literacy, with a published syllabus and past problems.

Top scorers from the online rounds are invited to further rounds and team selection.

Syllabus and past problems online
Online rounds in spring 2027

The Informatik-Biber is the entry point to Germany's family of computing competitions run by BWINF: short interactive tasks on algorithms, logic and data, no programming required. Teachers register their school and run the test in class during the Biber weeks.

Interested students can continue with the Jugendwettbewerb Informatik (from spring, for beginners in programming) and the Bundeswettbewerb Informatik, which leads to IOI selection.

en: Free, in class, no coding needed
Grades 3–13
Gateway to Germany's informatics olympiad track

eligibility.en: Students in grades 3–13 at schools in Germany (and German schools abroad), registered by a teacher.

en: Ask a teacher to register the school on bwinf.de
Try past Biber tasks

The Primary Kangaroo is an open-entry multiple-choice challenge designed to make problem solving fun for younger pupils. Schools choose a day in the window and run it in class; certificates are awarded to top scorers.

It is a natural first step before the Junior Mathematical Challenge.
